claims.text: Comprehensive, intensive behavioral interventions (≥26 contact hours) in children and adolescents 6 years and older who have obesity can result in improvements in weight status for up to 12 months.
There is inadequate evidence regarding the effectiveness of weight management interventions with less than 26 contact hours in children and adolescents.
The harms of behavioral interventions for obesity in children and adolescents can be bounded as small to none.
The harms of screening for obesity in children and adolescents are minimal.
Screening for obesity in children and adolescents 6 years and older is of moderate net benefit.

evidence.description: Comprehensive, intensive behavioral interventions (≥26 contact hours) in children and adolescents 6 years and older who have obesity can result in improvements in weight status for up to 12 months
there is inadequate evidence regarding the effectiveness of less intensive interventions.
The harms of behavioral interventions can be bounded as small to none
the harms of screening are minimal.
Therefore, the USPSTF concluded with moderate certainty that screening for obesity in children and adolescents 6 years and older is of moderate net benefit.

methodologies.name: USPSTF Systematic Evidence Review
methodologies.description: Systematic review of evidence on screening for obesity in children and adolescents and the benefits and harms of weight management interventions.
conditions: children and adolescents aged 6 years and older

limitations.text: There is inadequate evidence regarding the effectiveness of less intensive behavioral interventions (<26 contact hours).
